title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame topology) framework. The structure has four ingredients.
- A set F of 'figures', with two relations: ≤ (sub-figure) and ≪ (a 'strict' or interior inclusion).
- A set M of elementary figures ('multistructures').
- A set L of points ('lieux').
- A comparison map p_F: F → Fig(L), sending a figure to its underlying set-theoretic multi-stratified figure ('multens(F)').

The previous page shows that this map is increasing for ≤ and ≪ and commutes with Sup and Inf, but need not be injective. This page continues the examples, to show that the converse properties fail in natural situations. That motivates the next page's definition of an 'atelier ensembliste', in which p_F is injective and reflects ≤, ≪ and incompatibility.

Example 1B (simplicial):
- M is the set of pairs (A,σ), where A ⊂ E (E a topological space), σ is an affine-simplex structure on A, and the inclusion A → E is continuous. Each pair gives a set-theoretic figure Φ_σ (the stratification by open faces) with support A.
- (A',σ') ≤ (A,σ) iff (A',σ') is a sub-simplex (face) of (A,σ).
- (A',σ') ≪ (A,σ) iff Φ_σ' ≪ Φ_σ in Fig.
- Compatibility: (A,σ) and (A',σ') are compatible iff A∩A' is empty or a common face of both.
- F is the set of finite (or locally finite) subsets of M that are closed under taking faces and pairwise compatible. In other words, F is the set of (locally) finite geometric simplicial complexes continuously injected in E.
- Again L ≅ E. The map M → Multistrat(L) ⊂ Fig(L) is not injective once E contains an arc [0,1]: different affine parametrizations of the same arc give the same face stratification. So the set-theoretic shadow forgets the PL/affine structure.

Example 2 (pseudodisk):
- Take a 'pseudodisk' (B,∂B,...) in E, of combinatorial type 'disk with a marked point' (picture ⊙).
- The corresponding figure is not determined by the open part B∖∂B together with the contractile 'centre'. One must also give a 'neighbourhood structure' at the boundary, i.e. something like a germ of collar.

Conclusion: it is 'sans doute illusoire' to hope that multens(F) ≤ multens(F') ⇒ F ≤ F', or likewise for ≪. The next page says the opposite actually holds in examples 1A and 1B, and then defines ateliers and morphisms of ateliers.

Purpose: to separate 'set-theoretic' (ensembliste) ateliers, which are faithfully represented by stratified subsets of the point set, from structured ones (PL, simplicial, collared) where figures carry extra data. This is a step toward an axiomatics of tame/modérée topology as envisaged in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: Notational slip: the compatibility clause says 'face commune de (X,σ) et (X',σ')'; it should be (A,σ) and (A',σ').
Compatibility should also require that the affine structures induced on the common face by σ and σ' coincide. This is implicit in 'face commune' but not stated.

Only continuity of A → E is required, so the simplices need not be embedded topologically: their topology can be finer than the induced one. This makes non-injectivity even more severe than the [0,1] example suggests. It is not an error, but it is a looseness in the definition.
Example 2 is only sketched: the 'structure de voisinage' at the boundary is not defined.

ideas.what: Abstract 'atelier': a set of figures with sub-figure order ≤, strict/interior inclusion ≪, and a compatibility relation, mapped to set-theoretic stratified figures on a point set.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; loosely akin to region-based/point-free topology (contact/proximity algebras, mereotopology) and o-minimal-type structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Contact algebras: de Vries (1962), Whitehead/Tarski. o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86). Grothendieck's 'ateliers' are not credited anywhere that I know of.
ideas.where_published: The tame-topology programme is sketched in the Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the specific 'atelier' axiomatics appears unpublished.

ideas.what: Simplicial example: (locally) finite families of continuously injected affine simplices, closed under faces and pairwise meeting in common faces, as figures of a space E.
ideas.modern_name: Geometric simplicial complexes in a space / triangulated subspaces

ideas.what: Observation that the forgetful map to set-theoretic stratifications is not injective (reparametrized arcs) and does not reflect ≤ or ≪.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness failure of the forgetful functor from PL/structured figures to stratified sets

ideas.what: A pseudodisk's figure needs, besides its interior and 'centre', a neighbourhood ('collar') structure along the boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Collar / germ-of-neighbourhood data, as in stratified spaces with control data (Mather) or mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods (Quinn)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (1969–70), Brown collaring theorem (1962), Quinn homotopically stratified sets (1988)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's framework closely parallels later point-free/region-based topology, though the literature never connects the two. It has a lattice of figures with ≤, a strict containment ≪, compatibility/disjointness, and representation of the abstract structure by subsets of a point set ('atelier ensembliste' = faithful representation).
missed.quote: (A',σ') ≪ (A,σ) ⇔ Φ_σ' ≪ Φ_σ ; ... il est sans doute illusoire d'espérer que multens(F) ≤ multens(F') ⇒ F ≤ F'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The parallels are with de Vries contact algebras, proximity spaces, way-below in continuous lattices, and Stone-type representation theorems. Making the comparison explicit could give the unpublished 'ateliers' a precise place: as a representation problem for contact-like algebras of tame figures. It is also relevant to current tame-geometry axiomatics (o-minimal, Shiota's tame structures).

missed.claim: The pseudodisk example indicates that a correct notion of figure must include boundary neighbourhood ('collar') germs. This is never formalized here.
missed.quote: il faut en plus se donner une "structure de voisinage" de a au bord ....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is essentially the problem of control data and germs of neighbourhoods in stratified/tame topology. Comparing it with Quinn's or Hughes' homotopically stratified framework could clarify what Grothendieck's 'modérée' programme intended.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly routine examples, motivating a definition on the next page. What is notable is the unpublished axiomatic 'atelier' structure itself (≤, ≪, compatibility, faithful set-theoretic representation), part of the little-known 1986 Analysis situs project, and its unstated kinship with point-free topology. No deep new theorem appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'sous-simplexe [-(face)-] de (A,σ)' — 'de (A,σ)' is written above as an insertion; '(face)' appears to be kept in parentheses rather than struck.
'𝔏_σ' ≪ 𝔏_σ' is most likely Φ_σ' ≪ Φ_σ (the set-theoretic figure of the simplex, as on p.34).
The compatibility symbol is a crossed comparison-type sign (like ≶ or ≬), not ⋔. The same sign appears on p.36 as the third relation, transcribed there as '≰'.
'(par ex. si E contient une partie homéomorphe à [0,1] !)' — the image reads more like '(par ex. si E contient [0,1] !)'.
'multicont(F)' is uncertain. Given p.36, it is probably 'multens(F)' (multi-ensembliste); the struck word at the start of that line looks like 'Mult multens(F)'.
'structure de voisinage de ∂ au bord' — the image reads '"structure de voisinage" de a au bord ....'
